slot.brief: A merry-go-round or turntable with a person walking from rim to centre; apply conservation of angular momentum to find the new angular speed and kinetic-energy change.

stem: A person of mass $2$ kg stands at the rim of a turntable of moment of inertia $6$ kg m$^2$ and radius $1$ m. The system rotates at $3$ rad s$^{-1}$. If the person walks to the centre, find the new angular speed and the increase in rotational kinetic energy. Treat the person as a point mass.

verdicts.working: Initially, I = 6 + 2(1)^2 = 8 kg·m², so angular momentum is 8(3) = 24 kg·m²/s. At the centre, I = 6 kg·m², giving ω = 24/6 = 4 rad/s. The kinetic-energy increase is ½(6)(4²) − ½(8)(3²) = 12 J.

working:
$I_i=6+2(1)^2=8\ \text{kg m}^2$, $I_f=6\ \text{kg m}^2$
$L_i=I_i\omega_i=8(3)=24\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$
$\omega_f=\dfrac{L_i}{I_f}=4\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$
$\Delta K=\dfrac{L_i^2}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{I_f}-\dfrac{1}{I_i}\right)=12\ \text{J}$

Independent check: Initially, I = 6 + 2(1)^2 = 8 kg·m², so angular momentum is 8(3) = 24 kg·m²/s. At the centre, I = 6 kg·m², giving ω = 24/6 = 4 rad/s. The kinetic-energy increase is ½(6)(4²) − ½(8)(3²) = 12 J.
solution:
With no external torque, angular momentum is conserved. $I_i=6+2(1)^2=8$ and $I_f=6\,\text{kg m}^2$.
$$\omega_f=\frac{I_i\omega_i}{I_f}=\frac{8(3)}{6}=4\,\text{rad s}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta K=\frac12(6)(4^2)-\frac12(8)(3^2)=12\,\text{J}$$
